descriptor: Pre-revenue lithium developer · 40%-carried JV stake in Puna Mining S.A. (Rincon project, Argentina) · reported in AUD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Argosy has no revenue and no operating cash inflow — both lines are corporate overhead plus advances funded into the Puna Mining JV. Net income swings sharply on non-cash impairment/reversal entries on the JV investment (FY2024: A$10.8m impairment on the H1 write-down of A$69.4m; FY2025: A$10.1m reversal), not on operating performance.

sections.title: JV Funding & Impairment (Puna Mining)
sections.subtitle: Argosy holds Rincon through a 40%-carried, equal-board equity-accounted JV it cannot fund alone. These lines are the funding relationship and the non-cash swings on it, not operating performance.

charts.title: Advances to Puna Mining vs JV Carrying Value
Impairment Expense vs Reversal (Puna Mining Investment)
charts.annotation: FY2024's A$10.8m full-year figure follows a A$69.4m H1 write-down partly offset in H2; FY2025's A$10.1m reversal is the main reason FY2025 reported a net profit. Both are non-cash marks on the JV carrying value, not cash earned or lost.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Argosy Minerals Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

jvFunding.title: Puna Mining JV funding
jvFunding.content:
Argosy jointly controls Puna Mining S.A. (equal board representation, majority votes needed for material decisions) and equity-accounts for it rather than consolidating it — so none of Rincon's project economics show up as Argosy revenue or costs. Advances to Puna Mining is cumulative cash Argosy has funded into the JV (an amount owed back to it); the JV investment is that funding's carrying value after Argosy's share of Puna's losses and any impairment/reversal; exploration & evaluation assets is Argosy's own directly-held tenement carrying value.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: Argosy cannot build the 12ktpa Rincon project alone — the DCF assumes a farm-down leaves Argosy a ~40% carried interest. Rising advances with a carrying value that keeps pace show the JV is being funded without being written down; advances growing faster than the JV investment is the JV burning cash faster than its assessed value is rising.

What to watch:

  • Advances rising while the JV investment stalls or falls (funding not reflected in value)
  • Exploration & evaluation assets growing separately from the JV — Argosy's own directly-held ground
  • A signed farm-in/offtake-with-funding partner, which the DCF treats as the key re-rating catalyst

impairment.title: Impairment and reversal (JV investment)
impairment.content:
Under equity accounting, Argosy tests its Puna Mining investment for impairment each period. An impairment expense writes the carrying value down (usually on a weaker project outlook, funding delay or lower commodity-price assumption); an impairment reversal writes some of it back up if the outlook improves. Both are non-cash and can dominate reported net income for a pre-revenue company with no operating profit to offset them.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: H1 FY2024 booked a A$69.4m impairment (full-year A$10.8m after a partial H2 offset); FY2025 booked a A$10.1m reversal, which is the main reason FY2025 shows a positive EPS/net income in the KPI cards above. Neither year reflects a change in cash generation — Argosy still has no revenue.

What to watch:

  • A reported profit year that coincides with an impairment reversal rather than new cash flow
  • The assumptions behind the carrying value (commodity price deck, discount rate, project timeline) disclosed in the impairment note
  • Whether swings track news on funding/FID for Rincon, which is what actually drives the JV's value

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: Argosy is pre-revenue at the consolidated level, so there is no gross profit or operating income line — the whole story is net income, which is dominated by non-cash movements on the equity-accounted Puna Mining investment. H1 FY2024 booked a A$69.4m impairment on that investment (full-year A$10.8m after a partial offset); FY2025 booked a A$10.1m reversal, flipping the year to a small reported profit. Neither reflects an operating turnaround — look at the JV funding cards, not this chart, for the real progress signal.

What to watch:

  • Impairment/reversal swings on the Puna Mining carrying value (see JV Funding section)
  • Whether a reported profit year coincides with an impairment reversal rather than cash generation

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Argosy Minerals Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
